main_text.p: Etenim ex verbo Dei agnoscimus CHRISTUM obdientia & morte sua expiasse peccata nostra, & nos effuso[?] suo sanguine in remissionem peccatorum DEO reconciliasse, & non modo hoc effecisse, verum etiam impetrasse nobis Spiritum sanctum, regeneratem nos per vocationem efficacem, illuminantem mentes nostras fidejustificante, & voluntatem nostram excitantem ad studium bonorum operum, ut sicut ipse Christus excitatus postea est ex mortuis in gloriam patris, ita & nos in novitate vitę ambulemus, ut enervetur corpus peccati, ne posthac serviamus peccato. Novimus enim sanguinem Christi purgare conscientiam nostram à mortuis operibus ad serviendum Deo vivo; & Christum peccata nostra pertulisse in corpore suo super lignum, ut peccatis mortui, justitiæ viveremus.
f. Absurdum per illam satisfactionem omne pietatis studium exstingui.V. Absurdum: & praeparatio ad alteram hujus Assertionis partem.
Aliud malum, ex affirmata Christi satisfactione, pullulat, ꝗ[?] omnium est nocentissimum, nimirum omne pieta-

page.notes: The note marker "f" is not visible in the text block; the note is placed beside the paragraph it stands next to. The top-left page number is faint and uncertain. The first paragraph may continue from the previous page, but no indent or prior words are visible, so it is not marked cont. The abbreviation before "omnium" is unclear and was written as ꝗ[?]. The "effuso" reading is doubtful. The catchword "tis" is the completion of "pieta-tis" on the next page. Show-through at the right edge is excluded.
